title: Legislative districts of Misamis Oriental

{{Short description|none}} {{Use Philippine English|date=May 2023}} {{Use mdy dates|date=May 2023}} {{Politics of the Philippines}} The '''legislative districts of Misamis Oriental''' are the representations of the [[Provinces of the Philippines|province]] of [[Misamis Oriental]] in the [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various national legislatures]] of the [[Philippines]]. The province is currently represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the [[Congress of the Philippines]] through its [[#1st District|first]] and [[#2nd District|second]] congressional districts. [[Camiguin]] and [[Cagayan de Oro]] last formed part of its representation in 1969 and 1972, respectively. == History == {{further|Legislative district of Mindanao and Sulu|Legislative districts of Misamis}} Prior to gaining separate representation, most areas now under the jurisdiction of [[Misamis Oriental]] were represented under the former province of [[Misamis (province)|Misamis]] (1907–1931). Exceptions are territories which were annexed in 1921 from [[Bukidnon]] and thus formed part of the [[Legislative district of Mindanao and Sulu|representation]] of the [[Department of Mindanao and Sulu]] from 1917 to 1922: Napaliran (annexed to [[Balingasag, Misamis Oriental|Balingasag]] in 1921), [[Claveria, Misamis Oriental|Claveria]] (became a municipality in 1950),{{cite web |title=Executive Order No. 334, s. 1950 — Converting the Municipal District of Claveria, Province of Oriental Misamis, into a regular municipality |url=http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/1950/07/22/executive-order-no-334-s-1950/|last=Magsaysay|first=Ramon|date=July 22, 1950|access-date=November 21, 2017|website=Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines}} Lourdez (distributed between [[Alubijid]], [[El Salvador, Misamis Oriental|El Salvador]], [[Initao]], [[Manticao]] and [[Opol, Misamis Oriental|Opol]] in 1955){{cite web|title=Executive Order No. 96, s. 1955 — Merging the municipal district of Lourdez in the Province of Misamis Oriental with the municipalities of Alubijid, El Salvador, Initao, Manticao and Opol, same province|url=http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/1955/02/09/executive-order-no-96-s-1955/|last=Magsaysay|first=Ramon|date=February 9, 1955|access-date=November 21, 2017|website=Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines}} and Lumbia (distributed between [[Cagayan de Oro]] and [[Opol, Misamis Oriental|Opol]] in 1954).{{cite web|title=Executive Order No. 38, s. 1954 — Merging the Municipal District of Lumbia in the Province of Misamis Oriental with the Municipality of Opol, same province, and the City of Cagayan de Oro|url=http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/1954/05/26/executive-order-no-38-s-1954/|last=Magsaysay|first=Ramon|date=May 26, 1954|access-date=November 21, 2017|website=Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines}} The approval of Act No. 3537 on November 2, 1929, split the old Misamis Province into [[Misamis Occidental]] and [[Misamis Oriental]], and provided each successor province a separate representative in the [[Philippine Assembly]].{{cite journal|author=Philippine Legislature|title=Public Laws enacted by the Philippine Legislature during the period August 9, 1929 to February 7, 1930 comprising Acts Nos. 3529 to 3672|journal=Public Resolutions, Etc |series=Laws, etc |date=1930|publisher=Bureau of Printing |url=https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=mdp.35112102880772;view=1up;seq=119|access-date=November 18, 2017|format=Digitized and uploaded by University of Michigan on March 9, 2016}} The new province of Misamis Oriental first elected its [[#Lone District (defunct)|own representative]] in the [[1931 Philippine House of Representatives elections|1931 elections]]. The province also remained part of the [[Senatorial districts of the Philippines#Eleventh District|eleventh senatorial district]] which elected two out of the 24-member [[Senate of the Philippines|upper house]] of the [[Philippine Legislature]] when senators were still elected from territory-based districts until 1935. During the [[Second World War]], the Province of Misamis Oriental sent [[#1943–1944|two delegates]] to the [[National Assembly of the Second Philippine Republic|National Assembly]] of the Japanese-sponsored [[Second Philippine Republic]]: one was the provincial governor (an [[ex officio member|''ex officio'' member]]), while the other was elected through a provincial assembly of [[KALIBAPI]] members during the [[Japanese occupation of the Philippines]]. Upon the restoration of the [[Philippine Commonwealth]] in 1945 the province retained its pre-war [[#1931–1969|lone congressional district]]. Even after receiving their own city charters, [[Cagayan de Oro]] and [[Gingoog]] remained part of the representation of the Province of Misamis Oriental by virtue of Section 90 of Republic Act No. 521 (June 15, 1950){{cite web|url=http://laws.chanrobles.com/republicacts/6_republicacts.php?id=525|date=June 15, 1950|author=Congress of the Philippines|website=Chan Robles Virtual Law Library|access-date=November 18, 2017|title=Republic Act No. 521 – An Act Creating the City of Cagayan de Oro}} and Section 89 of Republic Act No. 2668 (June 18, 1960),{{cite web|url=http://laws.chanrobles.com/republicacts/27_republicacts.php?id=2672|date=June 18, 1960|author=Congress of the Philippines|website=Chan Robles Virtual Law Library|access-date=November 18, 2017|title=Republic Act No. 2668 – An Act Creating the City of Gingoog}} respectively. The passage of Republic Act No. 4669 on June 18, 1966, separated the sub-province of [[Camiguin]] from [[Misamis Oriental]] and constituted it into an independent province; per Section 4 of the said law, the [[#1931–1969|incumbent representative for Misamis Oriental]] continued representing the new province until its [[Legislative district of Camiguin#Lone District|separate representative]] was elected in the [[1969 Philippine House of Representatives elections|November 1969 elections]].{{cite web|title=Republic Act No. 4669 - An Act separating the Subprovince of Camiguin from the Province of Misamis Oriental and establishing it as an independent province|date=June 18, 1966|access-date=November 19, 2017|author=Congress of the Philippines|website=Chan Robles Law Library|url=http://laws.chanrobles.com/republicacts/47_republicacts.php?id=4673}} Misamis Oriental was represented in the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]] as part of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region X]] from 1978 to 1984. The province returned [[#1984–1986|two representatives, elected at large]], to the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]] in [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election|1984]]. [[Cagayan de Oro]] separately elected its [[Legislative districts of Cagayan de Oro#At-Large (defunct)|own representative]] starting that year. Under the new Constitution which was proclaimed on February 11, 1987, the province was reapportioned into two congressional districts;{{cite web|title=1987 Constitution of the Philippines - Apportionment Ordinance|website=Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines|url=http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines-ordinance/|author=1986 Constitutional Commission|date=February 2, 1987|access-date=November 19, 2017}} each elected its member to the restored [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|House of Representatives]] starting [[1987 Philippine legislative election|that same year]]. == Current districts == Misamis Oriental's current congressional delegation is composed of two members since 1987.
